b: Mike Xavier posted an excellent comment to Rick Connor’s recent post regarding paying off his mortgage in order to reduce what he needed to earn in order to maintain the same lifestyle.
Determining what we can afford while working should be pretty simple. We know what we earn, so we should know if we have enough to make the payments on whatever it is that we want to buy.

Things can get a little more complicated when we give up our job and the reliable paycheck that came with it. Take the case of a retiree and vagabond wannabe, whose dream it is to buy a motorhome and travel the country. What if his new hotel-on-wheels comes with a $1000 monthly payment, $12,000/year. Assuming that guaranteed income sources such as SS and pension are not sufficient to pay the obligation, how much nest egg is needed to generate that payment?
Based on a 4% withdrawal strategy, $300,000 would be required to service a $1K monthly payment. ($12000/.04).
Considering the sorry state of the typical retirement account, it seems that not many retirees should be carrying any debt at all. And for those still employed, you better get saving.
